critical.issue: db.payouts has a legacy unique index on event_id (line 5731: `await db.payouts.create_index('event_id', unique=True)`). companion payouts insert with event_id='' so the SECOND companion booking that reaches accept/confirmed anywhere in the DB throws pymongo.errors.DuplicateKeyError inside companion_payout(), which bubbles out of fulfil_order and returns HTTP 500 from /api/payments/verify. On a fresh DB this happens the very second time any two members ever complete + accept — production-blocking. Fix: convert the index to partial (partialFilterExpression={'kind': 'event'} or {'event_id': {'$type': 'string', '$ne': ''}}), OR store companion payouts in a separate collection, OR drop the unique index entirely and rely on companion_payout()'s own booking_id de-dup guard.

moderate_companion() sets `companion.enabled = state=='approved' AND doc.companion.enabled` where doc is the PRE-update document. When a companion is suspended enabled is written to False; on subsequent re-approval doc.companion.enabled is still False, so re-approve leaves enabled=False and the companion never re-appears in GET /api/companions. Reproduce: suspend Ananya, approve Ananya, GET /api/companions — she is missing even though her status is 'approved'. Fix: set enabled=True on approve (or preserve enabled only across non-approve transitions).

critical_code_review_comments: server.py:5731 — Unique index on payouts.event_id is a legacy assumption from before companion payouts existed. Any collection you store multiple payout kinds in needs a partial or compound unique index.
server.py:5662 — Boolean AND with old value silently disables a re-approved companion. Approve should be idempotent and restorative.
server.py:5460 fulfil_companion — awaits notify() (which sends email) inline in the payment-verify request path. A slow provider stalls the checkout for the member. Consider asyncio.create_task.

server.py:1381 price_for('companion') — returns tax_pct=18. Companion services shouldn't necessarily be taxed at product-GST 18% (they might be a person-to-person service outside GST scope). Confirm with finance before launch.

server.py:5387 create_booking — computes `amount = max(listed, offer_amount)` but does NOT cap the offer_amount, so a member could book at ₹10 crore and legitimately owe payment. Add a sensible ceiling (e.g. offer <= 3x listed, like counter-offers).

server.py:5586 complete_booking — either party can mark complete, but does not require the OTHER party's confirmation. A dishonest companion could self-mark 'completed' after showing up briefly to bump their completed count. Consider requiring member-side confirmation.

server.py:5479 grant_credit — writes an unbounded number of credit rows without an idempotency key on the booking, so a companion who declines, is un-declined (via admin), and re-declines would double-credit. There is no admin 'un-decline' today, but the pattern is fragile.
server.py:5507 my_bookings — no pagination beyond .limit(100). A prolific companion could easily exceed that and lose visibility of old bookings. Add pagination.
server.py:5320 list_companions — no rating/completed sort options despite storing both fields; sort is hard-coded to hourly_rate asc.

server.py:5479 grant_credit — sends an email inside every credit issuance and is awaited in the request path; on a burst (e.g. cron-driven mass no-show handling) this will queue behind Resend rate limits.

rca_of_the_issue: Bug 1 (payouts 500): startup() line 5731 creates `db.payouts.create_index('event_id', unique=True)` from the event-payout era. When companion_payout() inserts with event_id='', the SECOND such insert violates the unique constraint (both rows have event_id=''). fulfil_order calls companion_payout() inside /api/payments/verify, so the user sees a 500 during checkout. Fix: partial index `{'event_id': {'$gt': ''}}` OR compound (event_id, kind) OR separate the ledger. Bug 2 (approve-after-suspend): the `AND` in `state == 'approved' and doc.companion.enabled` reads the pre-write value of enabled — which suspend just set to False — producing enabled=False on the very next approve. Reproduction: suspend Ananya via /api/admin/companions/{id} {action:'suspend'}, then approve; GET /api/companions and she's not there. Fix: `enabled = True if state=='approved' else (doc.companion.enabled and False)` or simpler: always enable=True on approve.
